name: Koita
catalog_citation: Dutton, T.E. 1975. A Koita Grammar Sketch and Vocabulary. In T.E. Dutton (ed.), Studies in Languages of Central and South-East Papua, Pacific Linguistics C-29, 281-412. Canberra: ANU.
catalog_locator: p.286, section 1.21 Orthography (PDF page 6 of sealang); supporting remark on stressed-vowel length p.285
catalog_quote: Word stress (marked ´) is contrastive in Koita: ómo head v. omó adze, gúdi digging stick v. gudí lime, gúma path v. gumá axe, and is accompanied by lengthening in the stressed vowel. In phrases, however, stress position and strength may change according to the effects of morphophonemic rules discussed below, e.g., magí íahu > magíahu old woman and word stress may be reduced to fit the whole pattern. For example if " indicates primary stress and ' secondary stress then 'era "ba'tara that's a moon > 'era 'bataya"bara those are moons. Details of these shifts have not been studied for this sketch; neither have intonational and pausal features which are related to it.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage is verbatim on p.286 of the held sealang PDF of Dutton 1975a (page image read), with the p.285 vowel-length remark also present. (2) Deciding source is a 1975 Pacific Linguistics grammar sketch by the language's sole first-hand describer; Glottolog's descriptive bibliography has nothing better (n_desc_refs=1), and Dutton 2010 (fetched sources, CC BY) both confirms 'stress is typically contrastive in all of the [Koiarian] languages... described in detail [for] KTA' and shows no later published Koita phonology exists (only his unpublished 2007 dictionary ms). Dutton 1969 (fetched sources) predates and defers on Koita stress. (3) The LEXICAL coding with no positional default and the phrase-level caveat faithfully reflects the source; nothing found suggests a recode. Koita is a shifting language near Port Moresby with no SIL programme listed by Dutton, so an instrument

sources.citation: Dutton, Tom. 2010. Reconstructing Proto Koiarian: The history of a Papuan language family. Pacific Linguistics 610. Canberra: ANU. 126 pp. hdl 1885/146757, DOI 10.15144/PL-610, CC BY 4.0.
sources.quote: 'Stress is typically contrastive in all of the languages although generally not described in any detail, except for KTA [Koita], KOI and BAR(N). ... Intonation has not been studied in detail in any of the languages except KOI (Dutton 2003). For the above reasons stress and intonation are not taken into account in reconstructing the proto forms.' The only Koita sources Dutton lists are Dutton 1969, 1975a and his own unpublished ms. 'A dictionary of Koita' (2007).

sources.note: Describer's own 2010 family overview; p.8 confirms stress is contrastive in Koita and that 1975a is the detailed description. Now held.

sources.citation: Dutton, T.E. 1969. The Peopling of Central Papua: Some Preliminary Observations. Pacific Linguistics B-9. Canberra: ANU. 198 pp. hdl 1885/146442, CC BY-SA 4.0.
sources.quote: 'Vocoid glides are interpreted as sequences of vowels, although in Koita, Mountain Koiari, and Barai this needs further investigation together with the interpretation of stress. In the three languages of the Family studied in more detail (viz., Koiari, Aomie, and Managalasi) stress has been found to be phonemic. None of the Koiarian languages is tonal.' The Koita section (5.83.2) gives phoneme contrasts only, no stress rule; superseded by Dutton 1975a.
